library: causal-learn, in-repo copy (externals/causal-learn); GPU path: externals/acceleration/pc (accelerated_pc)
assumptions: Causal sufficiency (no unmeasured common causes), faithfulness, acyclicity, i.i.d. samples, Markov property.
output: CPDAG (codes 1 directed, 2 undirected, 3 bidirected; 2/3 stored above the diagonal)
notes: GPU code is used only if CUDA is present and indep_test contains 'gpu'; on CPU only '_cpu' is stripped, so a '_gpu' name reaches causal-learn unchanged. The GPU path ignores background knowledge and returns the matrix as raw_result. If CUDA is present but the acceleration package is missing, the import fallback calls an unimported logger (NameError at import). Puts externals/causal-learn first on sys.path. The hyperparameter file also describes background_knowledge, but only primary parameters reach the wrapper.

library: causal-learn, in-repo copy (externals/causal-learn) (appended to sys.path; pc.py, imported first, has already put it first)
assumptions: Acyclicity, Markov condition, faithfulness; does not assume causal sufficiency (hidden common causes allowed).
output: PAG (codes 1 directed, 3 bidirected, 4 circle-arrow, 6 circle-circle)
notes: CPU only, no acceleration branch. raw_result is the tuple (graph, edges). Background knowledge supported in code but not a primary parameter.

library: causal-learn, in-repo copy (externals/causal-learn); GPU path: externals/acceleration/cdnod (accelerated_cdnod)
assumptions: Markov and faithfulness; distribution shifts across domains come from changes in causal mechanisms, not system-wide confounding; no fixed functional form.
output: CPDAG over the data columns (codes 1, 2, 3); the domain node's row and column are cut off
notes: Needs a 'domain_index' column; if missing it prints a message and adds a column of ones. Same _gpu/_cpu suffix handling as PC. Prints the converted matrix to stdout.

assumptions: unclear (no profile in context/algos, no tag entry, no hyperparameter file)
output: CPDAG (codes 1 and 2; undirected stored above the diagonal)
notes: gCastle's matrix is transposed into the repo convention and self-loops are cleared. cores of 16 or more is replaced by min(cpu_count, 14). With no profile or hyperparameter file it cannot be chosen through normal selection.

library: pyCausalFS, in-repo (externals/pyCausalFS, CBD.MBs.inter_IAMB); then causal-learn, in-repo copy (externals/causal-learn) via MB2CPDAG
assumptions: Causal sufficiency, Markov condition, faithfulness.
output: CPDAG-like merge of local PC graphs (codes 1 and 2)
notes: Runs the per-variable Markov-blanket search in parallel with joblib (n_jobs 4 by default), then MB2CPDAG (wrappers/utils/tab_utils.py) runs the in-repo causal-learn PC on each variable plus its blanket and merges the local graphs into one matrix (codes 1 and 2). The number of variables is counted before domain_index is dropped, so a domain_index column adds one target index that does not exist.

library: causal-learn, in-repo copy (externals/causal-learn) (FCMBased.lingam); GPU path: culingam
assumptions: Linear relationships, non-Gaussian errors (at most one Gaussian), acyclicity, causal sufficiency, independent errors.
output: DAG (0/1; LiNGAM's B[i, j] already means j -> i, so no transpose)
notes: Uses culingam only if CUDA is present and gpu=True (default False). If CUDA is present, gpu=True and culingam is missing, fit hits an undefined name. Weights are thrown away (any nonzero becomes 1). The causal order goes into info.

assumptions: No profile in context/algos; tab_tagging.txt tags it linear with non-Gaussian noise. Standard LiNGAM assumptions otherwise unclear from the repo.
notes: Tagged Unavailable. Weights are thrown away. Its hyperparameter file also lists random_state, which is not primary and is dropped.

library: PC or GES wrapper (in-repo causal-learn), then causal-learn ANM or PNL and Meek rules
assumptions: No profile in context/algos; tab_tagging.txt tags it flexible functional form, Gaussian noise, sparse graphs. Otherwise unclear.
output: Partly oriented CPDAG (codes 1, 2, 3); tagged DAG
notes: Stage 1 is PC or GES. For each undirected edge, stage 2 tries ANM/PNL direction tests with up to m_max candidate confounders, then applies Meek's rules, and repeats until nothing changes. GES ignores the alpha it is given. Prints each orientation. Tagged Unavailable.

assumptions: Linear relationships, Gaussian noise (somewhat robust), acyclicity within a time slice, causal sufficiency, stationarity.
output: Lagged graph: lag_matrix[lag, effect, cause] plus a summary matrix
notes: Maps causalnex node names back to columns assuming causalnex lists nodes variable by variable with exactly p+1 entries each; this ordering assumption is not checked. Also listed under score-based algorithms in wrappers/__init__.py.

library: tigramite (PCMCI.run_pcmciplus; ParCorr, RobustParCorr, GPDC, Gsquared, RegressionCI, CMIknn tests)
assumptions: Causal Markov condition, faithfulness, stationarity.
output: Lagged graph: lag_matrix[lag] with effect rows and cause columns, plus a summary matrix (any lag)
notes: Builds the graph only from p-values (p or FDR-corrected q <= pc_alpha) and ignores PCMCI+'s own oriented graph, so a same-time link sets both cells. GPDC runs on PyTorch if CUDA is present. An unknown indep_test leaves the test unset (UnboundLocalError). The hyperparameter file also offers link_assumptions, which is not primary.

library: causal-learn, in-repo copy (externals/causal-learn) (FCMBased.lingam.VARLiNGAM); GPU path: culingam.varlingam
assumptions: Non-Gaussian noise, linear relationships, stationarity, causal sufficiency.
output: Lagged graph of weights (lag_matrix not binarised) plus a 0/1 summary matrix
notes: gpu defaults to True. A compatibility subclass AcVarLiNGAMWrapper is defined but never used. If CUDA is present and culingam is not installed, the module fails at import.

assumptions: Linearity, Gaussian errors, stationarity, no same-time effects.
output: Summary matrix only (no lag_matrix, so results.lagged_graph is None)
notes: Pairwise ('pw', default) or multivariate ('mv') tests. Converts column names with int(), so it works only when columns are named '0', '1', ... Both modes put 1s on the diagonal.

assumptions: Nonlinear relationships through neural networks; acyclicity within a time slice, causal sufficiency, stationarity.
output: Lagged graph: lag_matrix[lag, effect, cause] (0/1) plus a summary matrix
notes: Standardises the data first. Uses CUDA if available. The number of lags p is not a primary parameter, so it stays at 10. Prints p to stdout.
